findings.reason: Plans to combine aliases from every provider for the same field, rather than using the first matching overlay’s aliases. This design accepts lower-priority aliases.
Proposes concatenating overlay providers and collecting all their aliases for a field. For overlapping field IDs, that violates first-wins-per-field behavior.

Again plans to iterate every alias provider and concatenate its results for one field, contrary to first-wins-per-field overlay behavior.
Plans provider concatenation while retaining aliases from both matching overlays for a field. First-wins-per-field requires the lower-priority overlay’s aliases to be ignored.
Adds StructureOverlay._merge_aliases as new + old without per-field winner selection; combined with the planned collection of every provider, overridden aliases remain usable.

Concludes that all non-mapping inputs now raise TypeLoadError based on tests with strings only. The earlier required-key membership checks still fail on integer input before reaching the guard.
Plans an overlay test that expects both recipes’ aliases for the same field to load. That tests the opposite of first-wins-per-field, under which the second recipe’s alias must not be accepted.
The overlay smoke test shows both x and y loading field a, and the agent accepts that outcome as correct rather than recognizing that the lower-priority alias should be ignored.
Reasons that both aliases from overlapping recipes should remain usable, overlooking that first-wins-per-field selects only the first recipe’s aliases for that field.
Again specifies an overlay test in which two recipes defining aliases for one field must both load successfully, encoding behavior contrary to first-wins-per-field.

Writes test_aliases_merge_from_multiple_recipes to assert that both x and y load field a despite the recipes defining that same field. The test would pass the incorrect overlay behavior reported by the official evaluation.
Rewrites test_aliases_merge_from_multiple_recipes with assertions that both overlapping aliases load the field. This again validates the behavior that the official first-wins-per-field test rejects.
